Belay 1.6.1

  • A rare overnight crash is fixed. With local diagnostics enabled, the log could grow heavier over time until a long night of agent activity caused Belay to crash. A detailed bug report helped track it down.
  • Set the timer by duration or end time. The custom timer now accepts either one and shows the other as you type.
  • Take your statistics with you. Before erasing your history, you can export every recorded day to CSV. Hover over the headline to see your time at the keyboard instead.

Also: chart bars now show their date on hover, disabled agent tiles dim consistently, the Off pill looks better in dark mode, shared statistics cards now attach correctly in more apps, and after an unexpected exit Belay records what happened in the log on the next launch.

Belay 1.6.0

  • Copilot CLI is now built in. Turn it on in Settings and Belay watches its sessions automatically. No folders to choose.
  • Watch built-in agents wherever they work. If an agent uses a custom config directory such as CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or you keep multiple profiles, open its settings and add the folders it uses. Precise Detection works across them too.
  • Your timer survives a relaunch. An Always On timer resumes with the same time remaining after Belay restarts.
  • More reliable throughout. A reliability pass fixed dozens of small issues, including launch stalls and sessions that stayed active longer than they should.

Also: agent tiles now show live last activity, disabled tiles dim consistently, and there’s a little more polish throughout the interface.

Belay 1.5.0

  • Cline is now built in. Turn it on in Settings and Belay follows Cline sessions on its own. No folders to pick.
  • Precise Detection for every agent. Claude Code, Codex, and Cline can tell Belay the exact moment work starts, finishes, or waits for you. One click in Settings; Belay shows exactly what it will write before touching anything, and Remove puts it back.
  • Agent teams in the panel. When Cline spawns teammate agents, they appear under their session, just like Claude Code subagents.
  • Settings, sharpened. Each agent’s detection now lives in its own tile, and every pane reads cleaner.

Also: sessions touched by other apps’ importers no longer wake the panel, the agent switches draw honestly from the first frame, and running the test suite can no longer disturb a running Belay.

Belay 1.4.0

  • Keep your Mac awake for a set time. Choose anywhere from 15 minutes to 12 hours below the mode picker. Belay shows how much time is left and lets your Mac sleep when the timer runs out.
  • Pick up where you left off. If a timer or your awake limit ends a hold, the panel tells you why and gives you a Hold Again button. Unlocking your Mac resumes the hold automatically.
  • See the countdown on the dimmed screen. When Belay dims the display at night, the time remaining appears in the centre of the screen.
  • Hear your week. Move across the chart in Statistics and each day plays a note. Busier days have a higher pitch.

Also: Claude Code and Codex now each have their own switch in Settings. Belay no longer asks for access to folders it will not use. The dimming setting now says when dimming actually happens, What’s New has a new card layout, and the panel no longer moves when you switch modes.

Belay 1.3.3

  • The panel stays in sync. Finished turns now go quiet within seconds and stay that way. No stale rows after restarts, no jumping back to Working, and the idle timer starts from when the session actually went quiet.
  • Codex crashes no longer linger. If Codex quits or crashes mid-turn, Belay notices the process is gone and lets go within seconds instead of waiting through the retry grace period.
  • The lid helper restores what it changed. It remembers your previous sleep setting and puts exactly that back. If you enabled disablesleep yourself, Belay leaves it alone.
  • Diagnostics are more useful. Every session transition and hook signal now gets one line in the local diagnostics log. Nothing leaves your Mac.

Also: late signals after a turn ends no longer keep the Mac awake for five extra minutes, opening the Codex app no longer floods the panel, and the lid-hold time limit is no longer affected by changes to the system clock.
